steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Accurate written description requires precise dance terminology, not everyday language

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Movement description should cover action, dynamics, space and relationships (A D S R)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Action vocabulary includes actions of the body: turn, jump, travel, gesture, fall, stillness

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dynamics describe how movements are performed: fast, slow, sustained, sudden, heavy, light

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the four key areas you should cover when describing dance movement? | Q: Give an example of describing dynamics accurately rather than vaguely. | Q: Why should you avoid subjective language like 'beautiful' in exam answers?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Action, dynamics, space and relationships (A D S R). Together, they provide a complete description of what happens, how it happens, where it happens and how dancers interact. | Vague: 'The dancer moved nicely.' Accurate: 'The dancer performed a sustained, slow développé with light, flowing quality, gradually extending through the leg and arm.' | Subjective language does not describe what actually happens in the dance. Examiners reward precise technical observation — describing dynamics, actions and spatial design — rather than personal opinio

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use A D S R (Action, Dynamics, Space, Relationships) as a checklist for complete descriptions Always pair a technical term with a specific example from the work you are describing Write in present tense: 'The dancer extends' not 'The dancer extended' Replace vague words with precise ones — 'sustained' not 'slow', 'percussive' not 'hard' Practise writing timed descriptions of short sections to build speed and accuracy
